answer: High-risk actions require two of the user devices to be online at the same time and both to sign the request within a short window. A remote attacker holding one device cannot satisfy the simultaneity check, and faking presence for many accounts means operating many live devices in parallel, which is costly to automate. One haven proves nothing on its own; the proof is in the whole pattern of continuity. After the garden closes and the kernel opens, the recovery is frozen and published for audit.
